scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: C2 assessment draft addressing conditional resilience, institutional responsibility and limits of metrics.

tabs.title: Qualified Interpretation
tabs.description: Distinguish the writer's precise claims and qualifications.

tabs.title: Argumentative Analysis
tabs.description: Examine implications, analogies and the limits of evidence.

tabs.title: Reasoned Judgement
tabs.description: Evaluate new educational situations using the writer's framework.

questions.q: When, according to the author, does resilience cease to be an unambiguously helpful ideal?
choices: When learners are encouraged to reconsider an assumption.
When effort produces only gradual rather than immediate results.
When it becomes an unconditional moral demand detached from circumstances.
When institutions acknowledge that recovering from setbacks can be difficult.
questions.explanation: The opening paragraph distinguishes resilience as a useful capacity from an unqualified obligation, especially under persistent constraints.

questions.q: Why might two pupils appear equally determined while having profoundly different educational experiences?
choices: One pupil's determination can be measured while the other's cannot.
Visible persistence does not show whether renewed effort has a reasonable chance of helping.
Equally determined pupils are likely to receive substantially different marks.
Determination necessarily depends on the resources available at home.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two contrasts visible effort with whether the learner's environment allows effort to produce meaningful change.

questions.q: What is the force of the author's claim that an indicator may not be 'false'?
choices: It reveals all important dimensions of educational success when interpreted carefully.
It becomes misleading only when pupils deliberately manipulate their scores.
It is neutral because every important learning outcome can eventually be quantified.
It may accurately measure a limited outcome while concealing other forms of learning.
questions.explanation: Paragraph three recognises that indicators can be technically accurate while missing exploration, judgement and other valuable learning.

questions.q: What is the significance of the contrast between retrospective inspiration and advising someone amid ongoing constraints?
choices: Advice offered during adversity must account for conditions that an uplifting finished story may obscure.
Stories about adversity are useful only when the protagonist has already succeeded.
People who face constraints rarely benefit from the examples of others.
Retelling successful experiences is a more reliable guide than assessing present resources.
questions.explanation: The opening paragraph distinguishes resilience as a useful capacity from an unqualified obligation, especially under persistent constraints.

questions.q: What conceptual distinction does the author draw between agency and endurance?
choices: Agency refers to innate confidence, while endurance is acquired through instruction.
Agency is always voluntary, whereas endurance is necessarily forced.
Agency entails the possibility of purposeful change, whereas endurance may simply mean surviving persistent obstacles.
Endurance is proof that support was sufficient to overcome institutional barriers.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two contrasts visible effort with whether the learner's environment allows effort to produce meaningful change.

questions.q: Why does the author introduce a system that tracks how rapidly scores improve?
choices: To illustrate how a valid metric may privilege familiar practice over difficult exploration.
To demonstrate that quick score improvement usually indicates shallow knowledge.
To show that all standardised assessments reward memorisation rather than understanding.
To propose a better way of comparing two equally motivated learners.
questions.explanation: Paragraph three recognises that indicators can be technically accurate while missing exploration, judgement and other valuable learning.

questions.q: Which possible misreading does the final paragraph explicitly resist?
choices: That schools should assess students only after they have rested.
That criticising resilience rhetoric means treating ability as fixed or denying learner responsibility.
That revising strategies is less valuable than improving institutional resources.
That the notion of success should be removed from educational decisions.
questions.explanation: The conclusion rejects fatalism, retains meaningful evaluation and advocates agency supported by institutions and freedom to reconsider goals.

questions.q: A school rewards pupils for never abandoning a project, even when its goal has become pointless. What criticism follows from the text?
choices: It is unfair because pupils should be allowed to choose their own grades.
It prevents pupils from measuring their performance accurately.
It implies that teachers should never encourage ambitious long-term projects.
It mistakes perseverance itself for sound judgement about worthwhile aims.
questions.explanation: Paragraph three recognises that indicators can be technically accurate while missing exploration, judgement and other valuable learning.

questions.q: An institution celebrates students who overcome inadequate support without changing the support system. What is the author's likely objection?
choices: The celebrated learners should receive higher marks than their peers.
Praise for endurance may conceal institutional responsibility for the obstacle.
Endurance is never a genuine quality deserving recognition.
Students should refuse any achievement that requires sustained effort.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two contrasts visible effort with whether the learner's environment allows effort to produce meaningful change.

questions.q: Which approach most closely reflects the author's preferred conception of educational success?
choices: Use persistence as the main measure of success but adjust rewards for disadvantage.
Replace all assessment with individual expressions of curiosity and well-being.
Require every learner to demonstrate improvement while exempting leisure activities.
Combine meaningful student choice, realistic support, critical evaluation of metrics and the freedom to reconsider aims.
questions.explanation: The conclusion rejects fatalism, retains meaningful evaluation and advocates agency supported by institutions and freedom to reconsider goals.
